hook: The Mechanics' Institute, on the lot the Institute bought in 1866; the building on it now is an Article 10 landmark.

parcel.note: Business addresses are usually deferred on this site; this page exists because the address was named in the prompting source. The parcel spans 57, 61 and 65 Post Street, and DBI files permits under all three numbers.

historic_status.reason: Article 10 Individual Landmark, Article 11 Individual, Historic Survey Result

historic_district.note: The parcel's coordinates fall inside no historic district; its protection is the individual Article 10 designation.

permits.description: second and third floors — individual study rooms built out on the third floor, finishes updated, walls and ceilings repainted, floors carpeted, woodwork stained, light fittings and casework replaced, and cooling added to the third-floor IT closet

in-kind masonry repairs to the east elevation — loose material removed from scaffolding, deteriorated plaster parge coat, loose brick tie-backs and lintels repaired in kind, and the windows painted in place
drywall around the windows repaired and replaced after water damage, with baseboards and carpet renewed in the affected areas
change of use from bank to bar at 65 Post Street — the commercial tenant space remodelled and its bathrooms made accessible
barrier removal — an accessible countertop added at the library checkout desk on the second floor

permits_note: Seven of the 104 filings on this parcel are shown; the rest are sign and street-space permits, revisions to the permits above, and the duplicates DBI files under 57, 61 and 65 Post Street.

historical_record.description: The Mechanics' Institute bought the lot it still occupies on Post Street.
The Mechanics' Institute was founded in the slump that followed the fall in gold production, to give under-employed miners, artisans and tradespeople somewhere to learn and meet.
